chunks: And Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from al-Ṣādiq, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he said:
"When one of you performs sajdah, then let him place his palms directly upon the ground, so that Allah may ward off from him the shackles on the Day of Resurrection."

key_terms.اللَّهَ: Allah, the One who grants protection and relief
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the ground, directly contacted in sajdah
key_terms.الْغُلَّ: the shackle or fetter that may bind on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.بِكَفَّيْهِ: with his two palms, referring to the hands placed in prostration
key_terms.سَجَدَ: performed sajdah, meaning prostrated in salat
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection, when people are raised and judged

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about placing the palms on the ground during sajdah?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs the worshipper in the manner of sajdah, specifically to place the palms directly on the ground during prostration. It also connects this devotional act to the afterlife, stating that Allah may thereby avert shackles from the person on the Day of Resurrection.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.929 - Ismail ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Al-Sadiq, from his father (as), who said:
"When any of you performs Sujood (prostration), let them place their palms directly on the ground, so that Allah (swt) may protect them from shackles on the Day of Judgment."
